newsitem.title: GERMANY: German builders see downturn continuing into 1998.
newsitem.headline: German builders see downturn continuing into 1998.

text.p: The German construction industry sees no end to the current downturn until 1998, the HDB industry association said on Monday.

HDP president Otmar Franz said construction output in the first quarter rose 2.3 percent from the year-earlier quarter to 97 billion marks, after adjustment for inflation, but orders fell a real 7.6 percent.
Demand for new building remains weak and jobs reduction in the sector continues, Franz said, according to the text of remarks prepared for delivery at a news conference.

Employment in the construction industry was 10 percent, or 128,000 jobs, lower than in the year-earlier quarter. Competition from foreign firms that pay lower wages could mean the loss of a further 80,000 jobs this year, he said.
